title: feat(app-shell): render a flow that ended with `outcome: 'refused'` as a Close-only notice
body:
Fixes #7707

Lane (3) of the maintainer ruling on objectstack-ai/objectstack#14945 (director seat, decision batch #42). Lane (1) is that same card (the `packages/spec` contract) and lane (2) is objectstack-ai/objectstack#15788 (`service-automation` honouring the outcome) — both referenced here without a closing keyword, since this pull request does not deliver either of them.

## Step zero — the installed-surface probe, with both controls lit

This card's release criterion is a three-layer pin-consumption gate, and the unlock of 2026-09-18T14:16Z measured layer ① alone and said so. Layer ③ was measured here, in this branch's worktree after a normal `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, resolving `@objectstack/spec` from `packages/types` (a package that declares it):

```
RESOLVED_FROM = packages/types (declares @objectstack/spec)
INSTALLED_VERSION = 17.4.0
--- flow end node legs (FlowNodeSchema.safeParse) ---
SUBJECT  outcome:'refused' + message: ACCEPTED  parsed.config={"outcome":"refused","message":"Refused: {record.name} is a duplicate"}
SUBJECT2 no outcome (default check): ACCEPTED  parsed.config={"outcome":"completed"}
CONTROL A plain end, no config: ACCEPTED
CONTROL B outcome:'BOGUS_CONTROL': REFUSED   invalid_value@config.outcome: Invalid option: expected one of "completed"|"refused"
EXTRA    outcome:'refused' with NO message: REFUSED  (the spec's own refinement)
EXTRA    message with outcome completed: REFUSED    (the other direction of the same pair)
--- run-status vocabulary ---
ExecutionStatus.options = ["pending","running","paused","completed","failed","cancelled","timed_out","retrying","refused"]
```

Control B refusing is what makes the subject's ACCEPTED a reading rather than a shrug — and it earned its keep: the FIRST run of this probe had every leg REFUSED, controls included, because `FlowNodeSchema` requires a `label` the probe was not sending. A double refusal on the control is a blind instrument, not an absence; the probe was repaired and re-run, and the output above is the repaired run.

`refused` is representable as a run status distinct from `failed`, and `AutomationResult` declares the carrier the runner reads: `refusalMessage`, "set when `status` is `'refused'` … absent on every other status", alongside `success` staying `true` and `successMessage` NOT being set. So layer ③ is TRUE on this branch and the stop condition did not fire.

## The premise was re-measured on this branch's base, not inherited

The census that found the defect ran on the 17.2.0 pin. Re-measured on `ab856ed30` with a throwaway probe (deleted before the commit — its readings are transcribed here and the permanent pins cover the same ground):

| reading | value on the base |
|:--|:--|
| `toast.success` calls after a refused resume | `[["Flow \"convert_lead\" completed"]]` |
| `onComplete` calls | 1 |
| refusal sentence present in the DOM | **false** — swallowed entirely |
| message-only screen renders Cancel + Submit | true |

The defect is live on today's tree, in exactly the shape the card describes: the user is told "this is refused", clicks Submit, and is told the flow completed — while the authored refusal never reaches the screen at all.

## What changed

`interpretFlowResponse` gains its own `refused` kind. Deliberately its own, not folded into either neighbour: folded into `failed` it would render as an error (destructive banner, error toast) for a flow that WORKED; left in `done`, which is where it landed before this arm existed, it is the reported defect. The message is read from the one member the contract declares for it, with no alias chain (commandment #0.1).

`FlowRunner` holds a refusal separately from a resume error — the two are different events that happen to share a disposition — renders the engine-rendered sentence as a plain, non-destructive notice, and reaches the terminal affordance it already had a route to: Submit withdrawn, a single Close, and for an `object-form` step `showSubmit: false` with Cancel reading Close. What it does NOT do is as ruled as what it does: no toast of either colour, no `onComplete`, no invalidation.

`completed` runs are untouched. `silent` is untouched: a paused run still returns `{ success: true, silent: true }` and `silent` still suppresses the invoking action's `successMessage` at the runner's toast sink — that part already worked, and is pinned here rather than changed.

## Pins, and the ablation

Six pins in `FlowRunner.refusedOutcome-7707.test.tsx`: per-record text on a two-record fixture (each record's sentence asserted PRESENT and the other's ABSENT, which is what makes it a per-record measurement rather than two copies of one), no Submit and no Cancel with a footer Close, zero `toast.success` and zero `toast.error` calls with `onComplete` never called, the `completed` arm unchanged as the lit control that proves the toast spies fire at all, and `silent` through the real `ActionRunner` sink with its own lit control (the same action minus `silent` DOES toast its `successMessage`).

Reverse verification, direction predicted before running: deleting the `refused` arm from `interpretFlowResponse` must turn pins 1–3 RED while the `completed` control and both `silent` pins stay GREEN, and the RED must NAME the swallowed sentence. Run through `ablation-replace.mjs`, so the mutation is proven on disk rather than by an exit code:

```
ablation-replace:   anchor hits 1 time(s), as declared
ablation-replace: anchor   x1 -> x0
ablation-replace: blob     44a3dac3c5a3a05d76505e3c96b45d3794ba28a3 -> 2533ff567c4a1047ff5996b3ab7689e913f75f36
ablation-replace: ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob 44a3dac3c5a3 -> 2533ff567c4a
   x shows the sentence the engine rendered FOR THAT RECORD, for each of two records
   x withdraws Submit and offers Close only — the run is terminal and never resumed
   x fires NO toast at all, and does not report the run complete
 Tests  3 failed | 3 passed (6)
TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element with the text: Refused: Acme Corp is a confirmed duplicate
ablation-replace:   blob after restore  44a3dac3c5a3a05d76505e3c96b45d3794ba28a3
ablation-replace:   blob at HEAD        44a3dac3c5a3a05d76505e3c96b45d3794ba28a3
ablation-replace:   git diff HEAD       empty
ablation-replace: ok restored: blob == HEAD (44a3dac3c5a3) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```

Observed direction matches the prediction, the RED names the sentence, and the restore is proven by blob hash AND an empty `git diff HEAD` (trap on EXIT/INT/TERM against an absolute path is the tool's own).

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` — exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the new test file is type-checked too). It first read as red with `TS2307 Cannot find module '@object-ui/core'`, which is a PREREQUISITE NOT MET and not a verdict: the workspace closure was unbuilt. `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter "@object-ui/app-shell^..." build` first, then the type-check above.
- Targeted vitest: the six new pins, plus the seven existing flow files (`FlowRunner.*`, `flowResponse`, the `#2958` envelope ratchet, `useConsoleActionRuntime`) — 8 files, 102 tests, all green.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the final file list, verbatim:
  ```
  ✅ NOT GOVERNED — 4 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.
     An ordinary pull request: the normal review and merge-queue route applies.
  ```
- 16 further gates derived from this diff, each exit 0: `check:control-bytes` · `check:i18n-keys` · `check:i18n-drift` · `check:phantom-deps` · `check:self-import` · `check:spec-symbols` · `check:handler-key-reads` · `check:new-line-citations` · `check:vi-mock-specifiers` · `check:vi-mock-inherit` · `check:vi-mock-override-shape` · `check:test-path-roots` · `check:unreferenced-sources` · `check:changeset-claims` · `check:pending-changeset-literals` · `check:installed-pin-claims`. Plus `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, exit 0.

### Lint: NOT narrowed

`pnpm exec eslint . --no-inline-config --format json` ran over the whole tree at this branch's head — **5145 files linted**, no narrowing to declare. The three files this change touches carry **0 errors**; their warning sets are byte-identical to the same files' warning sets at the base (`flowResponse.ts`: one `no-explicit-any`; `FlowRunner.tsx`: three `no-explicit-any` plus the pre-existing `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` on the effect this change adds a sixth `setState` to; the new test file: 0 / 0), measured by linting the base blobs of both modified files under the same config. This change therefore adds no lint finding.

### Test narrowing: declared

The full `packages/app-shell` suite does NOT fit the foreground cap — `timeout 520 pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/` was killed at 520s, which is **NOT MEASURED**, neither green nor red. What ran instead:

- **Population** — every test file under `packages/app-shell/src` whose source names one of the five modules that can reach this diff: the two changed modules (`utils/flowResponse`, `views/FlowRunner`) and their three non-test importers (`hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx`, `views/RecordDetailView.tsx`, `views/index.ts`), enumerated with `git grep -l` — **plus** every test that imports the package barrel rather than naming a module, added so a load-time observer is not missed.
- **Count** — 62 + 9 = **71 files, 729 tests, all passing**.
- **Invariance** — neither changed module is part of the package's public surface: `interpretFlowResponse` and `FlowResponseOutcome` are not in `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` and no other package or app in the tree imports either name (both read from the tree, not assumed). `FlowRunner` IS exported, but its props are byte-unchanged — nothing was added to `FlowRunnerProps`. So a test outside this population cannot load the changed bytes, and no importing package is owed a test.

CI runs the full farm, including the whole `app-shell` suite and the repo-wide gates this dispatch did not enumerate.

## Acceptance notes

- **The LAUNCH path still swallows a refusal, and it is out of this card's ruled scope.** A flow that ends `refused` WITHOUT ever pausing at a screen never opens `FlowRunner` at all: `useConsoleActionRuntime`'s and `RecordDetailView`'s flow handlers fall through to their terminal-success tail and return `{ success: true, data }`, so the `ActionRunner` toasts the action's `successMessage` and the authored refusal is never shown. That is unchanged by this pull request, deliberately — leg (3) of the ruling names `FlowRunner`, and the clause "the invoking action's `successMessage` stays suppressed exactly as today (`silent`)" describes the paused-launch route, which is the only one that reaches this component. Reported for the seat to file rather than fixed here.
- Adding the `refused` arm does not disturb those two handlers: both check `failed` then `paused` and then read `outcome.data`, which the new arm also carries, so their behaviour and their types are exactly as before.
- A `refused` run with an EMPTY `refusalMessage` renders the Close-only disposition with no notice text. That combination is refused at the authoring door by the spec's `end` config (proven in the probe above), so it is an engine defect rather than an authorable shape; no fallback copy was invented for it, because a new `t()` key would have to land in all ten locale packs to satisfy this repo's i18n gates. The disposition is keyed on the STATUS, not on whether the sentence arrived.
- The claim comment on this card carries no `Clause-②:` line, so there was none to copy into this body.
- No label applied: this repo names no dev-applied label, `skip-changeset` is forbidden here, and `needs:contract-review` is the seat's.

Draft on purpose, and left for the seat to land: objectui `AGENTS.md` tells a green non-governed pull-request author to self-merge, that clause and this dispatch conflict, the conflict is filed as objectstack-ai/objectstack#19128, and until it is ruled the stricter side applies.
